request.spec:
The trim rule now applies once over the whole tree: the consolidated due-total and overdue-total
leave out the single highest and the single lowest person's figure over all people of the tree
when three or more have one, instead of adding up each sheet's trimmed total. The consolidated
people count counts each person once across the tree: people whose names or aliases match (as names
are compared) are one person.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The trim rule now applies once over the whole tree: the consolidated due-total and overdue-total
leave out the single highest and the single lowest person's figure over all people of the tree
when three or more have one, instead of adding up each sheet's trimmed total. The consolidated
people count counts each person once across the tree: people whose names or aliases match (as names
are compared) are one person.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The change is in and all 4 tests in the e2e spec pass on `bin/e2e`.

**The requested change** (front end only; the consolidated figures are worked out in the browser):
- **Due-total and overdue-total:** these now collect every person's figure from every sheet in the tree and trim once, dropping the single highest and the single lowest when three or more people have one. People whose due-total is n/a are still skipped. Before, each sheet's already-trimmed total was added up. Two people who share a name stay separate figures here; the spec's numbers need that (9.00, not 7.00 if they were combined).
- **People count:** people whose name or any alias matches (case and outer spaces ignored) count once. This carries through chains, so if A matches B and B matches C, all three are one person.
- **Files:** `features/consolidated/ConsolidatedFigures.tsx`, plus `features/people/useSheetFigures.ts`, which now hands out each person's figures and shares its trim function.

**A second fix the test needed, outside the request:** scenario 3 was failing on an audit line. Saving a grade from the row (`person-inline-grade-save`) wrote `PERSON_EDITED … terms=20` even though the terms weren't touched. The cause was in `Person.editTerms` (`src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/person/Person.java`): it flagged terms as changed whenever the person's base terms differed from the terms in force on the sheet's today. Ben has terms of 20 dated from 2026-03-12 and no base terms, so every save counted as a terms change.

Now terms count as changed only when the saved base terms differ from what the person had. That also applies to the full edit form and to people import, so a save that leaves the base terms as they were no longer writes a `terms=` field when dated terms are in force. Terms saved with a from-date are audited as before.
